tutorial: PartDesign_Hole.md (a Hole on a Pad's face: FreeCAD's ISO 273 clearance, ISO 4762 counterbore and ISO 10642 countersink sizes) for the bracket; CAM_Walkthrough_for_the_Impatient.md for the milled block (60 x 40 x 20 with a 30 x 20 x 8 pocket, as the CAM model of this pass). Neither page gives the bracket's sizes: an 80 x 40 x 10 plate is used. Make has no FreeCAD tutorial of its own (it is an add-on).

notCovered: printer_add, printer_send, printer_stop: they need a real printer on the network and the person's word; printer_list, printer_status and printer_pause are called only for their refusals
slice_open: it opens the slicer's window for the person (run it by hand after slice_with wrote the .3mf)
slicer_presets use / export / import / fetch: they need the person's own presets by name (list them first) and, for fetch, the network
thread_identify { scan }: needs ScanRuler-FreeCAD and a scanned thread
thread_cut mode modelled: slow and its volume is the helix's (tests/make/test_thread.py covers it, in a Body and in a plain solid)
hw_hole insert and magnet kinds, sketch and face inputs (tests/make/test_pdhole.py and test_stem_findings.py cover them)
dfm_check waive and part_review waive: they write a record from a tool listed as a read (see the findings)
fea_frame bodies: needs box-like BIM members
mass_calibrate with a real weight: needs a weighed print
